# wallix-bastion_configoption (Resource)

Provides a resource to manage options of a Bastion configuration file (e.g. `wabengine` for the
global configuration, `bastionadm` for the GUI, `rdpproxy` for the RDP proxy).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wallix-bastion_configoption" "global" {
  config_id = "wabengine"
  values = jsonencode({
    fqdn                  = "bastion.example.com"
    one_time_password_ttl = 60
    am = {
      session_timeout = 2000
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `config_id` (String)
- `values` (String, Sensitive)

### Read-Only

- `config_name` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `name` (String)

## Usage Notes

### Requirements

This resource requires API v3.12+ (WALLIX Bastion 12.3.1+). The `PUT /configoptions` endpoint is
a preview resource: the REST API option `preview_resources` (configuration `REST API`,
`wabrestapi`) must be enabled on the Bastion, otherwise the API returns `403 Forbidden` with
"Preview resources are not enabled in config".

### Configuration

`config_id` is the id or the name (`config_name`, e.g. `wabengine`) of the configuration file.
The name is the same on every Bastion, the id isn't. Changing `config_id` from the name to the id
of the same configuration, or the opposite, is not a change. The resource `id` is always the id of
the configuration.

### Values

`values` is a JSON object (use `jsonencode`) in the format of the API request body: an option of
a section is set in a nested object named after the section. The available options, their
sections and their types can be listed with the
[`wallix-bastion_configoption`](../data-sources/configoption.md) data source, or with
`GET /api/configoptions/<config_id>?metainfo=true`.

Only the options set in `values` are managed: the other options of the configuration file are
left unchanged and are not compared. If a managed option no longer exists on the Bastion, it is
removed from state and shows up as a diff.

Values are compared as JSON, so formatting and key order don't matter. The API checks the type of
each value, so the provider reads the type of the options before each update and adapts the numbers
set in `values`:

- a whole number is sent with a decimal point for a `float` option (`60` is sent as `60.0`): the
  API rejects `60`, and `jsonencode` never produces `60.0`;
- a number is sent as a string for a `string` or `option` (choice) option (`16` is sent as
  `"16"`), and is considered equal to the string read back.

Other types are not converted: a boolean must be set with `true`/`false`, not `"true"`. A section
must be set with an object of options (`banner = { type = "info" }`), and an option can't be set
with an object, otherwise the update fails before calling the API.

### Images

An option of type `image` (e.g. the GUI logos in `bastionadm`, section `oem`) is set with the
base64 content of the file, read with `filebase64`:

```terraform
resource "wallix-bastion_configoption" "gui_logo" {
  config_id = "bastionadm"
  values = jsonencode({
    oem = {
      logo       = filebase64("${path.module}/logo.png")
      logo_small = filebase64("${path.module}/logo-small.png")
    }
  })
}
```

The API only checks that the value is valid base64, not that it is an image of the expected type
(given by `help`, e.g. `Image (type: png)`, with `metainfo=true`): a wrong file is accepted and
breaks the display of the image.

### Destroy

The API can't delete a configuration file nor reset its options to their default value:
destroying this resource only removes it from state and leaves the options with their current
values on the Bastion.

Use only one resource per configuration file and set of options, otherwise resources overwrite
each other's values.

## Import

A configuration can be imported with its id or name (`config_id` is set to it), followed by the options to manage
(`<config_id>:<option>,<section>.<option>`):

```shell
terraform import wallix-bastion_configoption.global wabengine:fqdn,one_time_password_ttl,am.session_timeout
```

Importing with only `<config_id>` manages every option of the configuration file, including
images and other large values.
